## New variable creation based on existing variable

```{r Pop in 2030}
# To create new variable from existing when you are given initial population population (base of 2022 population size) growth rate(differ to each & every country),natural logarithm (2.71828) and time period(8 years.

time<- 2030-2022
world_pop$Pop_2030 <- world_pop$`2022 Population` *exp((world_pop$`Growth Rate` - 1) * 8)
names(world_pop)
sum(is.na(world_pop$Pop_2030))
```

# Extracting top ten countries with largest number of population

```{r top ten countries}
top_ten<-world_pop[order(world_pop$`2020 Population`,decreasing = TRUE),][1:10,]
top_ten

```
# By using ggplot2 

```{r graph of top ten}
# graph showing the visualization of countries vs population

ggplot(top_ten, aes(x = reorder(`Country/Territory`, `2022 Population`),
                  y = `2022 Population`)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(title = "Top 10 Countries by Population (2022)",
       x = "Country",
       y = "Population")
```


# Trend in population since 1990-2022 

```{r trend in population}
# The graph ggplot2 used to show the the trend of population since 1990 to 2022
trend <- pivot_longer(top_ten,
                      cols = c(`1990 Population`, `2000 Population`,
                               `2010 Population`, `2015 Population`,
                               `2020 Population`, `2022 Population`),
                      names_to = "Year",
                      values_to = "Population")

trend$Year <- as.numeric(substr(trend$Year, 1, 4))

ggplot(trend, aes(x = Year, y = Population, color = `Country/Territory`)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1990, 2000, 2010, 2015, 2020, 2022)) +
  labs(title = "Population Trend, 1990 to 2022 (Top 10 Countries)",
       x = "Year",
       y = "Population",
       color = "Country")
trend
```
## Extracting emission by top ten populous countries

# Handling missing values in co2_emission data_set

```{r fill}
# Step 1: Make a copy (this is my new data set)
co2_new_data <- as.data.frame(co2_emmission)

year_cols <- 5:34 # the year columns (1990 to 2019)

# Step 2: Fill the missing values in the copy only
for (i in 1:nrow(co2_new_data)) {
  row_values <- as.numeric(co2_new_data[i, year_cols])
  row_values[is.na(row_values)] <- median(row_values, na.rm = TRUE)
  co2_new_data[i, year_cols] <- row_values
}
sum(is.na(co2_new_data))
View(co2_new_data)
```

```{r drop}
co2_new_data$Totmissing <- NULL
names(co2_new_data)
```

# Dropping missing values after handling them by median computation

```{r Removing missing}
co2_emission_cleaned<-na.omit(co2_new_data)
sum(is.na(co2_emission_cleaned))
```


```{r Emmission}
# Since the top ten populous countries have been extracted above,let's keep only the countries which are most populated with their emission figure

top_ten_co2 <- co2_emission_cleaned[co2_emission_cleaned$country_code %in% top_ten$CCA3, 1:35]
top_ten_co2[, c(1, 5, 34)]
```

# Formatting the date (a row consist with country,year and CO2)

```{r Formatting}
co2_format <- pivot_longer(top_ten_co2,cols = 5:34,names_to = "Year",values_to = "CO2")
table(co2_format$`Country Name`)
```
# Keep clean number instead of text
```{r From text to numer}
co2_format$Year <-parse_number(co2_format$Year)
unique(co2_format$Year)
```
# Line graph showing emission trend since 1990-2019
```{r Trend of emission}
ggplot(co2_format, aes(x = Year, y = CO2, color = `Country Name`)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(title = "CO2 emissions of the 10 most populous countries\n(1990-2019)",
       x = "Year",
       y = "CO2 emissions (metric tons per capita)",
       color = "Country") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 11, hjust = 0.5,
                                  lineheight = 1.1,
                                  margin = margin(t = 10, b = 20)),
        plot.title.position = "plot",
        legend.position = "bottom")
```


```{r Corr}
# correlations between Area,Density,Growth rate, and World Population Percentage by using both numerical values and heatmap.

variables <- world_pop[,c("Area (km²)","Density (per km²)","Growth Rate","World Population Percentage")]
names(variables)<-c("Area","Density","Growth_Rate","World_pop_Percentage")
```
# Correlation as numbers
```{r}
cor_matrix <- round(cor(variables),2)
cor_matrix
```
# Correlation as heatmap
```{r corr}
Corr_format<-as.data.frame(as.table(cor_matrix))
names(Corr_format)<-c("Var1","Var2","Correlation")
ggplot(Corr_format, aes(x = Var1, y = Var2, fill = Correlation)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = Correlation)) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "darkblue", mid = "grey", high = "red",
                       midpoint = 0, limits = c(-1, 1)) +
  labs(title = "Correlation Heatmap", x = "", y = "") +
  theme_minimal()
```
# Choosing the columns we need

```{r kepp col}
pop_lation<-world_pop[,c("Country/Territory","2022 Population")]
names(pop_lation)<-c("Country","Population")

co2_2019<-co2_emission_cleaned[,c("Country Name","2019...34")]
names(co2_2019)<-c("Country","CO2")

```
# Merging these two tables by Country name
```{r merging}
merged_data<-merge(pop_lation,co2_2019,by="Country")
dim(merged_data)
```
# Graph of the emission with population
```{r plot}
plot(merged_data$Population,merged_data$CO2,
main = "Population VS CO2",
xlab = "Population(millions)",
ylab = "CO2 per person")
```
# Correlation of population vs CO2
```{r correlation}
cor(merged_data$Population,merged_data$CO2)
```

# Regression analysis
```{r regression_model}
model <- lm(CO2 ~ Population, data = merged_data)

tidy(model, conf.int = TRUE) |>
  gt() |>
  fmt_number(decimals = 3) |>
  fmt_scientific(columns = c(estimate, std.error, conf.low, conf.high)) |>
  tab_header(title = "Linear Model Results")
```

## Comparing emissions by continents
# Install & load package help on continent code

install.packages("countrycode")

# Join the continent column
```{r joining}
merged_data$Continent <- countrycode(merged_data$Country,
                                     origin = "country.name",
                                     destination = "continent")
```
# Check for missing
```{r missing check}
table(merged_data$Continent, useNA = "ifany")
merged_data$Country[is.na(merged_data$Continent)]
```
# Summation of CO2 by continent

```{r summation}
continent_co2 <- merged_data |>
  group_by(Continent) |>
  summarise(Total_CO2 = sum(CO2, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  arrange(desc(Total_CO2))

continent_co2
```
# Plot the data
```{r graphing of cont}
ggplot(continent_co2,
       aes(x = reorder(Continent, -Total_CO2), y = Total_CO2, fill = Continent)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(Total_CO2, 1)), vjust = -0.5) +
  labs(title = "Total CO2 Emissions by Continent, 2019",
       x = "Continent",
       y = "CO2 (metric tons per capita)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```
